clue.text: Orthodox priest taking pot shot at compiler

indicators.note: the priest is taking in, holding inside himself, the next piece

parts.note: Eli is the Old Testament priest who raised Samuel
a pot shot is a random stab at something
Shed is the name of the setter who compiled this puzzle

explanation.surface: A traditionalist cleric takes a swipe at the person who set the crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orthodox' looks like it describes the priest, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something orthodox is accepted and long settled, the sense of established practice.

clue.text: Means of suppressing dreadful shame and panic — seem cold

indicators.note: dreadful suggests something badly messed up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone tries to stay calm and look cool in spite of awful embarrassment and fear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadful' rearranges SHAME, PANIC, SEEM and C into the fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In psychology an escape mechanism is a way of avoiding or suppressing unpleasant reality.

clue.text: Drinks to the closure of "Spare Rib"

parts.note: cups of tea are drinks

indicators.note: the closure of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A round of drinks marks the end of the feminist magazine Spare Rib.
explanation.walkthrough: Spare Rib was a British feminist magazine; 'Rib' is split off as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To rib someone is to mock them playfully, a synonym.

clue.text: Wrap up the players on time

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another comes after it

parts.note: a band is a group of players of instruments
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: The musicians are told to finish up punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrap up' reads as finishing, but it means binding a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: To bandage a wound is to wrap it up in a strip of cloth.

clue.text: Stand that is designed as an alternative

indicators.note: something designed has been arranged into a new form

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A stand built for use as a substitute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges STAND plus IE.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing one thing instead of another is doing it as an alternative, a synonym.

clue.text: 24 natives pick up Soldier John, a ruffian

indicators.note: to pick something up is to take it in, so the natives contain the next piece

parts.note: 24 across is CHINESE, and the Han are the majority native people of China

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the piece is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
john is slang for a lavatory, as is loo

explanation.surface: Locals collect a soldier called John, a thug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pick up' splits: 'pick' takes in, and 'up' turns the soldier and John round to OOLIG in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooligan is a violent young troublemaker, a ruffian.

clue.text: Extract hypothetical element (deuterium) and accidentally gas the police with it

parts.note: D is the chemical symbol for deuterium

indicators.note: accidentally means things are thrown together by chance, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A chemist adds heavy hydrogen and gasses the officers by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accidentally' rearranges GAS THE POLICE and IT after D. Phlogiston was the hypothetical element once thought released in burning.
explanation.definitionFit: To dephlogisticate was, in old chemistry, to remove phlogiston, the imagined fire element.

clue.text: Germany's head correct about Germany? Only joking!

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
about means the correction goes around the next piece

parts.note: to edit is to correct
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A German leader puts something right about his country, then says he was kidding.
explanation.walkthrough: GEDDIT is a slangy spelling of 'get it?', said after a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Geddit? is said after a pun to flag it was meant in fun, like saying only joking.

clue.text: Earnest request for sportsperson to change sides

indicators.note: changing sides swaps left for right, the letter L for R

parts.note: a player is a sportsperson

explanation.surface: A petition for an athlete to transfer to another team.
explanation.definitionFit: A prayer is an earnest plea or entreaty.

clue.text: Impose restrictions on tea in leaderless African country

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other
leaderless drops the first letter

parts.note: Benin is a country in West Africa
cha is slang for tea

explanation.surface: Sanctions on tea in an African state without a ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaderless' leaves ENIN; tea as CHA is a crossword staple worth knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: To enchain is literally to put in chains, hence to restrict.

clue.text: Plug for Sunday hat

parts.note: a topper is a top hat

explanation.surface: Advertising a hat to be worn on Sunday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plug' suggests advertising, but it means a bung.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopper is a plug or bung for a bottle.

clue.text: Bad-mouth fresh crepe garnished with fruit

indicators.note: the crepe is garnished with fruit all round it, so the fruit goes outside

parts.note: a date is a fruit

indicators.note: fresh suggests something new made from the letters

explanation.surface: Criticising a newly made pancake topped with fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' makes EPREC; 'garnished with' tells you the fruit sits outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To deprecate is to disparage, or speak badly of, a synonym.

clue.text: Shed puts paid to the island

parts.note: the setter Shed speaks of himself as I
to put paid to something is to finish it, to slay it

explanation.surface: Something gets rid of the island.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as the setter speaking: Shed puts paid to, that is 'I slay'. ISLAY is a Scottish island famed for whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: Islay is an island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland.

clue.text: No more drinks on the magazine!

definitions.meaning: a British pub landlord calls ... when the bar stops serving

explanation.definitionFit: Calling time ends pub drinking, and Time is a well-known weekly news magazine.

clue.text: Admirer of Iron Maiden's "Number One Sausage"?

parts.note: the head is the number one, the person in charge
banger is British slang for a sausage

explanation.surface: A fan of a heavy metal band chooses a top sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: Iron Maiden is a heavy metal band, whose fans shake their heads to the music.
explanation.definitionFit: A headbanger is a heavy metal fan who nods violently to the music.

clue.text: On which to play song about fruit? On the contrary

indicators.note: about means one piece goes around the other
on the contrary turns it round, so the fruit goes about the song

parts.note: a melon is a fruit
an ode is a poem or song

explanation.surface: A tune circling a fruit, or maybe the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: As read, the song goes about the fruit; 'On the contrary' says the fruit goes around the song.
explanation.definitionFit: A melodeon is a kind of accordion, something played on.

clue.text: Recording of heartbeat broadcast during reception in New York?

definitions.text: broadcast during reception in New York?

indicators.note: a recording of a heart puts the heart word first

parts.note: ticker is slang for the beating heart
a tape is a recording

explanation.surface: Taping a heart beat, sent out at a New York welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: New York greets heroes with parades where paper strips are thrown from windows.
explanation.definitionFit: Ticker tape is the paper strip showered over New York parades.

clue.text: Appear nervous, supplying toe of newt to necromancer

indicators.note: the toe of a word is its last letter

parts.note: a witch practises necromancy and magic

explanation.surface: Looking jittery while handing a newt's toe to a sorcerer, as in a spell.
explanation.definitionFit: To twitch is to jerk nervously, a sign of anxiety.

clue.text: Twist of fate secures booze for East End pickpocket

indicators.note: secures means holds inside
a twist means the letters are rearranged

parts.note: ale is a kind of booze

explanation.surface: Fate sees a London thief locked up with drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twist of' rearranges FATE as TEAF, holding ALE. Tea leaf is London rhyming slang for thief.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang tea leaf means thief, used for a pickpocket.

clue.text: Fighting talk from European vermin (tailless)

parts.note: a Pole is a European from Poland

indicators.note: tailless drops the last letter

parts.note: mice are vermin

explanation.surface: Angry words from a European about mice without tails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailless' removes the E of MICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A polemic is an aggressive verbal attack, fighting talk.

clue.text: Ruler beginning to sink in pitch

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: tar is pitch

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A monarch starts to go under in black tar.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was the ruler of Russia.

clue.text: Weather-beaten but carpeted?

explanation.definitionFit: Rugged means weathered and rough; whimsically, covered in rugs like a carpet.

clue.text: Zeus's lover had returned in state

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Io was a lover of Zeus in Greek myth

indicators.note: returned means the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: Zeus's mistress got back into a state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' gives DAH; the Io of myth was a priestess turned into a heifer.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the fifty states of the USA, an example of the definition's class.

clue.text: One big, bland, blundering improvisation

indicators.note: blundering suggests clumsy disorder, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A large, dull person stumbles through an act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blundering' rearranges I, BIG and BLAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad-libbing is speaking or performing without preparation, improvisation.

clue.text: Looking up excerpt about Nabokov's language

indicators.note: in a down clue looking up means read from the bottom, backwards
an excerpt is a piece taken out of the words

explanation.surface: Searching for a passage about the novelist Nabokov's tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excerpt' takes UTNAB from 'about Nabokov's', and 'Looking up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Bantu is a large family of African languages.

clue.text: Language of novelist in church

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
Barry Hines is the novelist who wrote A Kestrel for a Knave

explanation.surface: The tongue of a writer inside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinese is the language of China.

clue.text: Must dialectal Scandinavian be so dull?

parts.note: mun is a northern English dialect word for must
a Dane is a Scandinavian from Denmark

explanation.surface: Asking whether a Scandinavian has to be boring.
explanation.definitionFit: Mundane means ordinary and dull.

clue.text: Produce fertiliser concealing universal truth

indicators.note: concealing means one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: manure is fertiliser
U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal
a fact is a truth

explanation.surface: Fertiliser hiding a universal truth.
explanation.definitionFit: To manufacture is to produce goods.
